item.title: Policy support, exporter resilience drive strong Oct trade performance: CII
item.description: The government's support and the strong efforts of exporters helped India's exports reach a record high of nearly USD 50 billion in October, CII's Sanjay Budhia said on Sunday. India's goods exports increased 45 per cent to USD 49.47 billion in October, compared to USD 34.11 billion in the same month last year. Imports also rose 16 per cent to USD 89.35 billion from USD 76.69 billion. As a result, trade deficit widened to a year high of USD 39.88 billion. Budhia, Chair - CII National Committee on Exports and Patton International's MD, said strong shipments of petroleum, electronics, engineering products and gems and jewellery pushed the country's shipments last month. "India's export performance for October is indeed encouraging and energising. It reflects the resilience, competitiveness and growing global footprint of Indian industry," he said. item.description: India and the US have sorted out the bulk of the issues relating to the proposed trade deal and it could be sealed "soon" as negotiations are underway to resolve the last stretch of concerns, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said on Saturday. His remarks come a month before Prime Minister Narendra Modi's likely visit to the US for the G20 Summit, on the sidelines of which he and President Donald Trump may meet to review the broader trajectory of bilateral ties and progress on the trade pact. In an interactive session at the HT Leadership Summit, the external affairs minister said the negotiations are approaching the "finishing line," adding that many of the remaining issues are "not so much at our end" and that more changes have occurred on the American side. item.title: Ficci calls for comprehensive India-Africa trade framework to boost ties
item.description: India and Africa should explore a broader trade arrangement as a more predictable framework could further boost trade, investment and economic cooperation between the two regions, industry chamber Ficci said on Saturday. item.title: India imports over half its edible oil, faces food risks: NITI Aayog VC
item.description: India is perhaps still not secure regarding its food supply across the various products, as the country is the world's largest importer of edible oils, NITI Aayog vice-chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri said on Friday. Addressing an event here, Lahiri said India meets more than half of its edible oil needs through imports, and imports are estimated at 17 million metric tonnes, valued at about USD 20 billion. Similarly, India is both the world's largest producer and consumer of pulses, and accounts for roughly a fourth of total global pulse consumption, approximately 25 to 27 million tonnes annually. "We are talking about Viksit Krishi in Viksit Bharat in 2047. As we move towards Viksit Bharat at 2047, are we secure regarding our food supply across the various products? Perhaps not as yet," he said. item.title: Moody's raises India's FY27 growth forecast to 7% on broad-based momentum
item.description: Moody's Ratings on Wednesday said the Indian economy is expected to grow at a higher rate of 7 per cent in the current fiscal, led by broad-based economic momentum and energy supply shock resilience. In its Global Macro Outlook 2027-28, Moody's, however, said that near-term risks to growth persist as household consumption remains vulnerable to "intensifying and broadening price pressures", with headline inflation close to the upper end of the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) 2-6 per cent target range, while a deficient southwest monsoon and strengthening El Nino conditions will weigh on agricultural output and rural demand. "India's broad-based economic momentum and demonstrated resilience to the energy supply shock warrant upward revisions to our 2026-27 growth forecasts to 7 per cent from 6.5 per cent," it said. Robust consumption, improving investment dynamics and strong macroeconomic fundamentals imply that the economy appears well positioned to sustain growth near 7 per cent over
item.bs:keywords: Moody's Ratings, India GDP growth, FY27 growth forecast, 7% growth, Indian economy, private investment, capital expenditure, inflation, El Nino, southwest monsoon, RBI monetary policy, energy supply shock
